newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-FROST LEADS MALAYSIA TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-FROST LEADS MALAYSIA TO VICTORY.

text.p: Morten Frost, the first European to coach in Asia, has his eye on the future after leading Malaysia to a first victory under his charge in the Sudirman Cup at the World Team badminton Championships on Tuesday.
The Dane, who took up a four year contract as Malaysian coach in February, was delighted to mark his debut with a 3-2 win over the Netherlands in Group 2B.

The result was achieved without Rashid Sidek, who was ranked world number one earlier this year. He is missing from the championships as the Badminton Association of Malaysia refused his request to play only in next week's individual events.

"It is a sad story that Rashid is not here," conceded Frost, a four time All- England Champion. "The BMA gave him plenty chances, but he turned them down. As a result, it is one chance less for Malaysia to win a medal. "But perhaps it is time to look to the future. This is a team for tomorrow. The women's ages range from 15 to 20, and they are did very well."
He was also delighted with the performance of another of his rising teenage stars, Yong Hock Kin, the world no 27, who defeated the experienced Chris Bruil 10-15 15-7 15-7 in the men's singles.

"It was his first major championship, and he did very well to win," Frost continued. "He has the potential to become a very good international player. It is now a case of transforming his performance in training into competitive situations."

Frost, who was based in England at the height of his playing career, took up the Malaysian appointment after over three years as Danish National coach. "It is a great honour to be the first European to go to Asia," he said. "I am finding it a tremendous challenge. "
